mekki-muskil:5-5.t:
His saying, the Exalted, {وَمن أضلّ مِمَّن يَدْعُو}: من is nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject); it is interrogative, and what follows it is its khabar (predicate). The third من is in the accusative position, governed by يدعو; it is in the sense of الذي (relative noun), and what follows it is its ṣila (relative clause).

His saying {إِمَامًا وَرَحْمَة}: two ḥāls (circumstantials) from الكتاب.

[Translator's note: إماما ورحمة is in āya 12, though it is printed under this entry.]

mekki-muskil:8-8.t: His saying {كفى بِهِ شَهِيدا}: accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) or as specification (bayān); به is the fāʿil (agent), and the bāʾ is redundant (zāʾida) for emphasis.

mekki-muskil:12-12.t:
His saying {لِسَانا عَرَبيا}: two ḥāls (circumstantials) from the latent nominative pronoun in مصدّق, or from الكتاب, because it has been given an adjective, مصدّق, and so approaches a definite noun, or from ذا; what governs the ḥāl is then the pointing or the drawing of attention (tanbīh). It has also been said that عربيا is the ḥāl and لسانا a preparatory element (tawṭiʾa) for the ḥāl.

His saying {وبشرى} is in the nominative position, conjoined to كتاب. It has also been said that it is in the accusative position as a maṣdar (verbal noun).

mekki-muskil:15-15.t:
His saying {بِوَالِديهِ حسنا}: its pattern is فُعْل, not فُعْلى, because فُعْلى is not fully declined, whether definite or indefinite; and moreover فُعْلى in a position like this is used only with the alif and lām. The accusative in it is because it stands in place of an omitted muḍāf, its implied form being "and We enjoined upon man, toward his parents, a matter possessed of goodness"; then the thing described was dropped and the adjective took its place, as He said {أَن اعْمَلْ سابغات}, i.e. "full coats of mail"; then the muḍāf, namely ذا, was dropped and the muḍāf ilayhi, namely حسن, put in its place.

Whoever read إحسانا put it in the accusative as a maṣdar (verbal noun), its implied form being "and We enjoined upon man, toward his parents, that he do good to them, a doing of good". He read as a maṣdar, its implied form being "and We enjoined upon man his parents, that he do good to them, a doing of good". [Translator's note: this sentence repeats the preceding one in the source, with «والديه» lacking the bāʾ; translated as written.] ʿĪsā ibn ʿUmar read حَسَنا with two fatḥas, its implied form being "a good deed".

His saying {وَحمله وفصاله ثَلَاثُونَ شهرا}: the basic rule for ثلاثين شهرا is to be accusative, because it is an adverb of time (ẓarf). But there is an omission in the speech of a ẓarf as muḍāf, its implied form being "and the term of his bearing and his weaning is thirty months"; so you predicate a ẓarf of a ẓarf. This is how the speech properly is: the mubtadaʾ (subject) is the khabar (predicate) in meaning. Were it not for this implied element, you would put ثلاثين in the accusative as an adverb; and had you done that, the meaning would be overturned and changed, and the enjoining would come to be within thirty months, as you say كلمته ثلاثين شهرا, i.e. "I spoke to him during this period". The meaning would be changed by that, so it was necessary to imply a ẓarf so that the intended meaning would be sound, because He, the Exalted, only intended to make clear how long the term of bearing and of weaning from suckling is. This verse shows that the minimum (term of) pregnancy is six months, because He, the Exalted, has made clear in another place that the term of suckling is two years, and has made clear here that the term of suckling and pregnancy is thirty months. If you subtract two years from thirty months, the term of pregnancy that remains is six months.

mekki-muskil:17-17.t:
His saying {وَيلك آمن}: ويلك is accusative as a maṣdar (verbal noun). It may be put in the nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject) with the khabar (predicate) omitted. With these maṣdars that have no verbs from their own root, the preferred (case) when they are put in construct is the accusative, though the nominative is permissible. That is why the readers are agreed on the accusative in His saying ويلكم لا تفتروا, and similar instances are many; the nominative is permissible in them. If they are not in construct, the preferred (case) for them is the nominative, though the accusative is permissible; that is why the readers are agreed on the nominative in His saying {ويل لِلْمُطَفِّفِينَ} and فويل لهم, and similar instances are many.

If the maṣdars are from verbs current upon them (i.e. having verbs of their root), then when they are definite the preferred (case) is the nominative, though the accusative is permissible, as in الحمد لله and الشكر للرحمن, a mubtadaʾ and khabar. If they are indefinite, the preferred (case) is the accusative, though the nominative is permissible, as in حمدا لزيد and شكرا لعمرو; this is the opposite of the first, so know it. Al-Mubarrad allowed only the nominative in His saying {ويل لِلْمُطَفِّفِينَ}, for a reason he mentioned.

His saying خلت النذر: النذر is the plural of نذير, like رسول and رسل. It may also be a noun for the maṣdar.

[Translator's note: خلت النذر is in āya 21, though it is printed under this entry.]

mekki-muskil:24-24.t: His saying {رَأَوْهُ عارضا}: the hāʾ in رأوه is for the clouds; it has also been said for the thunder (al-raʿd). What indicates it is His saying {فأتنا بِمَا تعدنا}.

mekki-muskil:26-26.t:
His saying {فِيمَا إِن مكناكم فِيهِ}: مَا is in the sense of الذي (relative noun), and إن is in the sense of the مَا of negation; the implied form is "and We had established them in that in which We have not established you". قد with the past is for expectation and nearness, and with the imperfect for paucity.

His saying {فَمَا أغْنى عَنْهُم سمعهم}: مَا is negating, and the object is من شيء, its implied form being "and it availed them nothing". It is also possible that مَا is interrogative, in the accusative position, governed by أغنى. The entry of من for emphasis shows that مَا is for negation.

[Translator's note: the source has «بأعني», evidently for «بأغنى».]

His saying {وحاق بهم مَا كَانُوا بِهِ يستهزؤون}: مَا is nominative, governed by حاق, and it together with what follows it is a maṣdar (verbal noun). In the speech a muḍāf is omitted, its implied form being "and the punishment of what they used to mock surrounded them", i.e. the punishment of their mocking, because the mocking itself does not befall them on the Day of Resurrection; only its punishment befalls them. This is frequent in the Qurʾān, as in His saying {فوقاه الله سيئات مَا مكروا}, i.e. the punishment of the evil deeds; and similarly {وقهم السَّيِّئَات وَمن تق السَّيِّئَات يَوْمئِذٍ}, i.e. "protect them from the punishment of the evil deeds, and whomever You protect from the punishment of evil deeds on that Day, You have shown him mercy"; and similarly {ترى الظَّالِمين مشفقين مِمَّا كسبوا وَهُوَ وَاقع بهم}, i.e. "and its punishment will fall upon them". The evil deeds themselves do not befall the disbelievers and fall upon them on the Day of Resurrection; only their punishment befalls them. So understand it.

mekki-muskil:28-28.t:
His saying {قربانا آلِهَة}: قربان is a maṣdar (verbal noun). It has also been said that it is a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose), and it has been said that it is the object of اتخذوا, with آلهة a badal (substitute) for it.

His saying {وَذَلِكَ إفكهم وَمَا كَانُوا يفترون}: مَا is in the nominative position, conjoined to إفكهم. الإفك is lying, and the implied form is "that is their lie and their fabrication", i.e. the gods are their lie and their fabrication. Whoever read أفَكَهُم made it a past verb, and مَا is again in the nominative position, conjoined to ذلك. It has also been said (it is conjoined) to the latent nominative pronoun in أفكهم; that is good because of the separation between them by the accusative pronoun, which takes the place of a tawkīd (emphasis).

mekki-muskil:33-33.t: His saying {بِقَادِر على أَن يحيي}: the bāʾ entered only according to the basic form of the speech, before the interrogative alif entered upon لم. It has also been said that it entered because in the speech there is a word of negation, namely {أولم يرَوا أَن الله}, so it was construed according to the wording rather than the meaning.

mekki-muskil:34-34.t: His saying {وَيَوْم يعرض}: يوم is accusative by an implied verb, its implied form being "and remember, O Muhammad, the day when (those who disbelieved) are exposed".

mekki-muskil:35-35.t: His saying {بَلَاغ}: nominative by an implied mubtadaʾ (subject), i.e. "this is a notification". Had it been accusative in (ordinary) speech, as a maṣdar (verbal noun) or as a naʿt (adjective) of ساعة, it would be permissible.
